svg.title: Generation benchmark: stage contracts and design review
svg.desc: Review of the attached pared-down design against the existing metric benchmark. Five numbered rows show each proposed stage's inputs, operation and outputs. Orange text marks dependencies or outputs missing from an explicit contract. Review notes identify missing independent stage invocation, measurement internals crossing boundaries, Docker lifecycle in the generic runner, hard-coded execution identities, and incomplete status handoffs. The footer recommends small artifact contracts and independent operations without adding a workflow framework.
svg.text: Generation benchmark: are the stages replaceable?
Review of the pared-down proposal • inputs, outputs, and the dependencies that cross each boundary
Verdict: reasonable scope; the handoffs need tightening before the five stages are independently replaceable.
Existing metric benchmark: copy this separation
Prepared cases + subsets
Execution
Indexed results + native evidence
Mutant scores / coverage scores
Correlation
Each stage has an API + standalone tool. Analysis can consume saved execution results. Native formats remain an explicit adapter concern.
Metric experiment: tests audit authoring. Generation experiment: tests task generation, using one fixed audit to measure coverage.
Each stage needs to run independently
Stopping after a stage is not enough. Specify how to run any stage on its own using saved inputs, through an API or a command.
WHAT IT NEEDS • source stages in brackets
WHAT IT DOES
WHAT IT PRODUCES • next stages in brackets
WHERE THE BOUNDARY NEEDS WORK
Establish coverage of the full task suite
Full task suite and evaluation agent
Execution settings
Behavior description (ETHOS)
Tool list and source versions
Case description
Create the fixed coverage audit.
Prepare the baseline case.
Run the agent on the full suite.
Also run the required nop control.
Measure coverage from saved trials.
Fixed audit and provenance: audit/ [2–4]
Task and agent bundle: baseline-case/ [3]
Indexed trial results: execution/ [2–4]
Full-suite coverage: coverage-full/ [3,5]
Complete when the audit validates and every evaluation-agent trial succeeds with a saved trace; retain the coverage receipt.
Keep the three operations replaceable
Creating the audit, running tasks and measuring
coverage can share one stage. Each still needs its own
callable interface.
Changing measurement should not require running the
agent again. The extra do-nothing run satisfies a
metric-specific manifest rule.
Allow each operation to consume saved inputs and produce
its own validated output.
Measure starting coverage for each task subset
Predefined task subsets
Indexed trial results [1]
Fixed audit and behavior description [1]
Case description
Fixed measurement settings
Select saved trials for each subset.
Measure the tools they cover.
Use the same fixed audit throughout.
Reuse recorded agent runs.
Subset coverage: coverage-subsets/ [3–5]
Coverage score and covered tool names
Reports and supporting measurements
Saved requests, responses and receipts
Combined score file: scores.json
Every subset has a validated response and receipt. When coverage cannot be determined, save the reason.
Publish results that other stages can use
Later stages read Eval Author’s report fields and
measurement folders directly. A replacement measurer
would have to imitate that layout.
A numeric score alone is insufficient: later stages also
need the tool names.
Export the score, covered and observed tools, audit identity
and evidence references in one validated format.
Generate new tasks for each subset with missing coverage
Subset tasks, agent source and trials [1]
Fixed audit and full-suite coverage [1]
Starting subset coverage [2]
Generator settings and supplied answers
ALSO NEEDED: subset membership and
held-out task content, for host-only leak
checks.
Give the generator permitted inputs.
Collect new tasks and logs.
Check baseline measurement
agrees.
Validate tasks and scan for leaks.
Keep held-out tasks on the host.
Tasks, logs and receipt: generation/ [4,5]
Validation decisions: gate/ [4,5]
Kept and dropped tasks, with reasons
ALSO NEEDED: a saved outcome for every
subset, including skipped and unavailable runs.
Distinguish no coverage gap, unavailable, completed with no tasks, and partially completed; keep held-out content out of the generator.
Let the generator own its runtime
The shared runner names and removes Docker
containers. Signing also requires an image. Requiring
baseline-report.json ties every generator to Eval Author
measurement.
Replacing Docker with a virtual machine would change
the shared interface.
The launcher should own isolation and cleanup. Keep Eval
Author’s local measurement inside its adapter.
Recheck generated tasks and measure expanded coverage
Validated generated tasks and digests [3]
Evaluation agent and execution settings
Saved trials and fixed audit [1]
ALSO NEEDED: subset membership,
starting coverage [2], case description and
generation outcome [3].
Recheck each generated task.
Require: reference solution scores 1;
do-nothing control scores 0;
evaluation agent finishes with a trace.
Combine old and kept new trials.
Measure their coverage together.
Recheck evidence: recheck/ [5]
Expanded coverage: coverage-plus/ [5]
Coverage report and receipt
ALSO NEEDED: kept and rejected task records;
an unchanged result if no tasks survive.
Every eligible subset has an expanded-coverage result or an unavailable reason. With no kept tasks, coverage stays unchanged.
Read identities from the results index
Combining old and new trials assumes names such as
case-0000 and agent-0000/run-0001. The metric results
format treats these as storage labels.
Another valid execution backend could choose different
names.
Follow indexed paths and task/agent identities. Preserve
each trial’s source and actual run identity.
Report how much missing coverage the generator recovered
Full-suite coverage [1]
Starting subset coverage [2]
Expanded subset coverage [4]
Covered and observed tool names [1,2,4]
Generation and recheck outcomes [3,4]
Audit identity and evidence receipts
Check all results use the same audit.
Check earlier coverage is retained.
Calculate the coverage gained.
Divide by the starting coverage gap.
Report the median recovery fraction.
Count every outcome.
Read saved artifacts only.
Final report: generation-analysis.json
Starting and expanded coverage
Coverage gained and recovery fraction
Median recovery fraction
Run status and rejected-task counts
Tools outside the audit; evidence links
Leave undefined recovery fractions unset. Account for every predefined subset using declared, validated inputs.
Save outcomes before summarizing them
Analysis needs rejection counts, reasons and evidence
references. Stage 4 currently specifies folders rather than
a complete outcome record.
Skipped runs and unchanged coverage also need saved
results.
Stages 3 and 4 should publish explicit outcomes so analysis
does not have to reconstruct what happened.
Keep the five stages; make their handoffs clearer
Recommended changes to the interfaces between stages:
A consistent coverage result
Save scores, tool names, the fixed audit identity and
evidence references together. Other stages should read this
result without knowing how the measurer stores its working
files.
An outcome for every subset
Save task identities, validation decisions, completion status,
reasons and supporting evidence. Publish an outcome even
when no tasks were produced or kept.
A way to run each stage on its own
Accept named input artifacts and write results to a new folder. Keep
the overall runner for convenience. Replacing a later stage should
reuse saved results from earlier stages.
Keep: the fixed audit, verified evidence, isolated generator workspace, independent host checks and one subset at a time.
Clarify: how the request reaches the generator, and how it saves accepted tasks before a timeout.
The current entrypoint writes response.json only at the end, while a missing response makes the entire run unavailable.
Reading guide: rows describe the proposal. Amber text marks missing inputs or outputs and suggested improvements.
Recovery fraction = coverage gained ÷ the gap between full-suite coverage and starting subset coverage.
• attached pared-down-design.md (Stages, Measurement, Generator command, Package layout)
Design review only: proposed generation implementation is not present in this checkout. Native Harbor evidence remains part of the existing metric contract.
